answer: Anchor every agent identity to a distinct, costly external credential — a domain name held for over a year, or a long-standing account on an unrelated platform — verified by an independent oracle. One credential anchors one identity. A Sybil farmer wanting a thousand identities must buy a thousand credentials, each priced in real money and time, while an honest agent already holds one. The kernel of the design is that the grove of identities feeds on nectar drawn from outside the system: trust is imported, not minted, so cloning inside buys no extra standing.
